title: st blend (starting)
parentNote: There is no new sound today. Back on day 31 your child learnt st on the END of a word — fast, lost, must — and today those same two letters move to the FRONT: stop, stick, stand, stuck. It is worth saying that out loud to them, because it is the whole lesson: same letters, same two sounds, other end of the word. A blend at the front is genuinely harder than one at the back, though, because the child has to hold /s/ /t/ in mind while the rest of the word is still arriving, and the usual slip is dropping the s altogether so stop comes out top. If that happens, cover the t and everything after it, get the hiss on its own, then uncover the rest.

activities.mouthCue: Hiss the s with your teeth almost shut, then tap your tongue down for the t.
activities.prompt: You already know this pair from the end of fast and lost. Today it moves to the front.
Three pairs that all start with a hiss. Find the one that ends with a tap.
Say the hiss and the tap on their own first, then push them together.
Now keep st in one piece. Three sounds: st, i, ck.
A blend on the front and a blend on the back.
The longest one. Four sounds and a t at each end.
One of these has an extra sound at the front. Listen before the vowel.
Same again. Is there a tap after the hiss?
Same start, same ending. Listen hard to the middle.

activities.text: Stop! The bus is stuck in the mud.
Sam did stand on a stump and did stomp.
Is the long stick still in the pond?

activities.title: Stuck on the hill
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: The bus is stuck in the mud on a big hill.
Gus did stomp and did stand at the back.
The bus did not shift. It is stuck fast.
A fat hog did run up and did jump in the bus!
The bus did tip and did pop up. It is not stuck!

questions.prompt: The bus is stuck in it.
It did jump in the bus and got it up the hill.
